name: read
description: Read a file, URL, or internal URI with path selectors for ranges (default 3000 lines). ssh://host/path is writable with `write` and searchable with `grep`; unsupported hosts: use `bash` with a remote SSH command or mount with `sshfs`.

path.description: File path, skill:// URI, URL; path selectors select a range.

name: write
description: Create or replace a file; use edit for small existing-file changes. Archive entries use archive.ext:path/inside (zip-family, tar-family, asar). SQLite rows use db.sqlite:table[:key], with JSON content for update and empty content for delete. xd://<tool> dispatches mounted devices with JSON content. Do not create documentation or emoji unless requested.

path.description: File path or writable internal URI; xd://<tool> dispatches a device.

name: bash
description: Run one command or short fact-producing pipeline in a persistent shell. Use cwd instead of cd; env for quoted/multiline values; pty only for terminal interaction. Order-dependent commands use &&. Prefer read for file contents/directories, glob for paths, grep for search, eval for scripts/complex control flow, hub start for long-running processes. Common shell utilities are available. Output is captured; truncated output links to artifact://. Internal URIs resolve to paths. timeout:0 disables the deadline.

timeout.description: timeout in seconds; 0 disables the command deadline; nonzero values are clamped to 1-3600

name: ask
description: Ask only when existing sources cannot resolve a choice with materially different user tradeoffs. Send related questions together; 2–5 concise options each, with tradeoffs in description. recommended is a zero-based default; multi allows multiple selections. Do not include Other: the UI adds it. Prefer action and state reasonable defaults when the choice is not material.

name: hub
description: Coordinate peers, background jobs, and project-scoped processes. The user is not a peer; Main answers in normal text. list discovers exact peer IDs (running/idle by default; status:'parked' for history). send({to,message}) wakes known peers; await:true waits for one reply (not with to:'all'); replyTo answers a message. inbox drains queued messages. Use paths, not pasted blobs. Do not message peers for facts tools can obtain. Jobs auto-deliver on completion. jobs snapshots; cancel({ids}) stops jobs. wait only when blocked: returns on the first matching message, job settlement, timeout, or interrupt; ids/from narrow it. User steering needs a text answer before another wait. Long-running services/watchers/REPLs use start({name,application,args,ready}), not bash. Readiness requires the supplied log/port checks, not mere process creation. ps/logs/wait/send/stop/restart/describe with name operate on that process. logs follow uses cursor; patterns are JS RegExp with u, not PCRE inline modifiers. stop is graceful before hard kill. persist survives the last OMP client; detached survives broker exit and disables PTY input. Omit unless needed. A settled job or process exit is not proof its artifact is accepted.

name: eval
description:
Run one step of code in a persistent kernel. State persists across calls and `task` subagents.
Eval `agent()` children use independent kernels.

Work incrementally: imports → define → test → use, each its own cell. Re-run setup ONLY after `reset`, kernel crash.
Two or more independent items → named `workpool()` + `.push(…)`; poll outside eval with `hub wait` on the pool name. Handles + `wait()` are for dependency-coupled results.

Top-level `await` works; `asyncio.run(…)` raises error.
JS runs under **Bun**: globals (`Bun.file`, `Bun.write`, `Bun.$`, `fetch`, `Buffer`) available; top-level `await`/`return` work.

On error, fix and re-run only the failing step.

<prelude>
Python: sync, kwargs. JS: async, ONE trailing object literal, never positional.
```
display(value) → None        print(value, ...) → None
read(path, offset?=1, limit?=None) → str
write(path, content) → str
env(key?=None, value?=None) → str | None | dict
output(*ids, format?="raw", query?=None, offset?=None, limit?=None) → str | dict | list[dict]
await tool.<name>(args) → unknown
    Invoke any session tool; `args` = its parameter object. Async: `await tool.read({...})`.
completion(prompt, model?="default"|"smol"|"slow", system?=None, schema?=None) → CompletionHandle
    Oneshot, stateless (no history/tools); returns immediately. `.wait()` → str (parsed object with `schema`). `model`: "smol" fast | "default" session | "slow" most capable.
agent(prompt, agent?="tiny-task", label?=None, schema?=None, schemaMode?="permissive", isolated?=None, apply?=None, merge?=None, tools?=None) → AgentHandle
    Spawns a background subagent and returns immediately. `agent` selects a discovered agent; omit it to use `tiny-task`. Allowed agents: `tiny-task`, `atomic-task-reviewer`. Handle: `.id`, `.handle` ("agent://<id>"), `.status`, `.done()`, `.wait(timeout?)` → final text (parsed with `schema`), `.send(message)`, `.cancel()`, `.output()`. Unwaited results auto-deliver like async jobs. `schema` overrides agent/session schemas; `isolated` requests a worktree; `apply`/`merge` control its changes. `tools`: names of your @tool-defined tools the child may call.
    JS: ONE trailing object — agent(prompt, { agent, label, schema, schemaMode, isolated, apply, merge, tools }).
wait(handles, timeout?=None, raise_errors?=True) → list
    Barrier over agent/completion handles, results in input order. `raise_errors=False` keeps the error in its slot. JS: wait(handles, { timeout, raiseErrors }).
workpool(agent?=None, name?=None, context?=None, tools?=None) → WorkPool
    Default for 2+ independent items. `.push(*items)`; `.status()`; `.peek()`; `.close()`. Pool name = async job id; results auto-deliver, or poll outside eval with `hub wait` and `ids:[pool.name]`. `eval.workpool.freshAgents=true` uses a new agent per item.
@tool / tool(fn, name=None, description=None)tool(fn, { name?, description?, parameters? })
    Define a tool that runs in this kernel (schema inferred from type hints); reference by name in `task` items' `tools`, `agent(tools=…)`, `workpool(tools=…)`. `tool.defined()`, `tool.undefine(name)`.
log(message) → None         phase(title) → None
budget → `budget.total` (ceiling or None), `budget.spent()`, `budget.remaining()``await budget.total()`, `await budget.spent()`, `await budget.remaining()`; ceiling `+Nk` advisory, `+Nk!` hard.
```
</prelude>
<dag>
Acyclic waves of handles:
- **Name nodes.** `h = agent(…)` returns at once; `h.handle` is `agent://<id>`.
- **Wire edges.** Put an upstream `.wait()` result or `.handle` in the downstream prompt. Bulk: `write("local://<name>.md", …)`.
- **`wait(hs)`** = wave barrier. Open-ended item streams → `workpool()`.
- **Isolate failure.** `wait(hs, raise_errors=False)` keeps a failure in its slot; only that subtree degrades.
- **Acyclic only.** No node waits on its own descendant.
</dag>

<critical>
Prior top-level names survive into the next cell — reuse; NEVER re-import/re-declare. Re-read only if file changed since last read.
</critical>

name: edit
description:
Single file string replacement; fuzzy whitespace matching.

<instruction>
- MUST use smallest `old_string` uniquely identifying change.
- Nonunique `old_string` → MUST add context or use `replace_all: true` for all occurrences.
- Rename a string across file → use `replace_all: true`.
- SHOULD edit existing files, not create new.
</instruction>

<output>
Success/failure status.
Success: file modified in place; replacement applied.
Failure — e.g., `old_string` absent or multiple matches without `replace_all: true`: error describes issue.
</output>

<critical>
- MUST read file at least once in conversation before editing. Tool errors on edit before read.
</critical>

<bash-alternatives>
Replace content-addressed — identify change by text.

Pattern-addressed bulk changes: bash more efficient:

|Operation|Command|
|---|---|
|Regex replace|`sd 'pattern' 'replacement' file`|
|Bulk replace across files|`sd 'pattern' 'replacement' **/*.ts`|

Use Replace when content identifies location; `ast_edit` for structure-aware codemods.
For in-place edits prefer Replace or `write` — diff preview and fuzzy matching.
</bash-alternatives>

name: task
description:
Run ONE subagent synchronously. Execution blocks until work finishes.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's most specific available agent. Omit `agent` when the spawn-policy default is the best fit; otherwise pass the specialist explicitly.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its agent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One-pass:** Prefer agents that investigate AND edit in one pass;
- **Overlap:** Parallelize independent ownership. Same-file edits are not guaranteed to merge. Name one integration owner and serialize only the irreducibly shared mutation boundary. Every concurrent batch has two prerequisites:
  1. Every task MUST skip validation (build/lint/tests) — validating mid-flight blocks agents on each other's edits.
  2. Decide cross-task contracts up front (e.g. the interface A implements and B consumes) and state them in the task, not left for agents to negotiate.

# Inputs
- `name`: A stable CamelCase identifier (≤32 chars), used to address the agent (IRC, job ids). Generated automatically if omitted.
- `agent`: The agent type to spawn (e.g. `reviewer`).
  Omitting `agent` selects the spawn-policy default (`task`). Use it only when that agent fits the task.
  NEVER pass the spawn-policy default explicitly. Only omit it after checking the available agents below.
- `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
- `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. Overrides the selected agent and parent-session schemas.
- `schemaMode`: `"permissive"` (default) accepts a retry-exhausted invalid result with a warning; `"strict"` fails it.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history.
Pass large payloads via `local://<path>` URIs, NEVER inline text.

# Format Contracts

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Available Agents
Agent spawning is currently disabled.
